quotes.text: there shall be a special commission to study and define conditions under which Single-Stair Multi-Family Residential buildings up to six stories shall be legalized in Massachusetts

The commission shall produce a building code amendment that allows single-stair multi-family residential buildings of up to six stories, including measures for mitigating any adverse health and safety impacts unique to single-stair multi-family residential buildings.

Said measures mitigating any adverse health and safety impacts would include general fire prevention measures, including smoke alarms, sprinkler systems, fire-resistant materials, emergency exit strategies, and any safety measures pertinent to 527 CMR 1.00.

The commission shall consist of the secretary of housing and livable communities, or their designee, who shall serve as chair, 2 members of the Massachusetts House of Representatives, or their designees, 2 members of Massachusetts Senate, or their designees

1 member representing the Fire Chiefs Association of Massachusetts, 2 members of the American Institute of Architects, 1 member who is a practicing fire engineer representing the National Fire Protection Association, 2 members representing the Board of Building Regulations and Standards

1 member representing the American Planning Association Massachusetts Chapter, 1 member representing the Home Builders and Remodelers Association, 1 member representing NAIOP, 1 member representing the Center for Building in North America, 1 member representing a building official employed by a municipality with a Class 1 Fire Department, and 1 member representing Abundant Housing Massachusetts.
The study shall build on the report Legalizing Mid-Rise Single-Stair Housing in Massachusetts produced by the Harvard Joint Center for Housing Studies, Boston Indicators, and Utile
a technical study into the safety of single-stair residential buildings compared to two-staircase buildings, and a process map and timeline for implementation of drafted building code amendment
Not later than July 31, 2026, the commission shall file its study with the clerks of the house of representatives and the senate and the joint committee on housing.

proposes.text: The bill would set up a special commission to study when apartment buildings of up to six stories with a single staircase could be allowed in Massachusetts.
The commission would write a proposed building code change allowing such buildings, along with steps to handle health and safety risks that are specific to them.

lines.text: It would study and define the conditions under which single-stair apartment buildings up to six stories could be legal in the state.
It would draft an actual building code amendment, not just a report.
The work would build on an existing report about mid-rise single-stair housing in Massachusetts.
The study would compare the safety of single-stair buildings with buildings that have two staircases, and would lay out a timeline for putting the code change in place.
The measures would include smoke alarms, sprinkler systems, fire-resistant materials, and emergency exit plans.
They would also cover safety rules tied to the state fire code section 527 CMR 1.00.

changes.heading: Who would sit on the commission

lines.text: The state housing secretary, or their designee, would chair it, with 2 members from the House and 2 from the Senate.
Fire chiefs, a practicing fire engineer from the National Fire Protection Association, architects, and the state building code board would each have seats.
Planners, home builders, commercial real estate, a municipal building official, and a housing group would also have seats.
The commission would file its study with the House and Senate clerks and the joint committee on housing.

affects.text: Builders, architects, planners, and fire officials would take part in writing the proposed code change.
Future apartment buildings of up to six stories could be built with one staircase if the code amendment were adopted.
A city or town with a Class 1 Fire Department would have a building official on the commission.

lines.text: If a code change like the one studied were adopted, apartment buildings of up to six stories with a single staircase could be built, which might change what housing is available over time.

notStated.text: The bill text does not mention tenants, leases, or evictions.

lines.text: The commission would draft a code amendment for single-stair multi-family buildings of up to six stories, which could affect what may be built on multi-family lots later.

notStated.text: The bill text does not mention zoning, property taxes, or existing houses.

lines.text: The secretary of housing and livable communities, or a person they pick, would chair the commission, so state staff could be assigned to the work.

notStated.text: The bill text does not mention pay, hours, or staffing for this work.

line.text: If it became law, the commission would have to file its study by this date.
